senses.definition: (obsolete, law) Someone who institutes a legal suit; a plaintiff or complainant.
(obsolete) Someone acting on behalf of someone else; a guardian.
Someone or something that takes part in some action; a doer, an agent.

quotes.text: A man may be principal in an offence in two degrees. A principal, in the first degree, is he that is the actor, or absolute perpetrator of the crime; and, in the second degree, he who is present, aiding, and abetting the fact to be done.
quotes.reference: 1769, William Blackstone, Commentaries on the laws of England^(https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File%3AWilliam_Blackstone%2C_Commentaries_on_the_Laws_of_England_(1st_ed%2C_1769%2C_vol_IV).pdf&page=48):

quotes.text: Never, my dear Bethel, did the most feverish dreams of fiction produce scenes more painful, or more terrific, than the real events to which I have been an actor, since the date of my last letter.
quotes.reference: 1792, Charlotte Smith, Desmond, Broadview, published 2001, page 373:

quotes.text: Mr. Clay had been too prominent an actor in public affairs to allow whig deception and misrepresentation a fair opportunity for successful action.

senses.definition: A person who acts a part in a theatrical play or (later) in film or television; a dramatic performer.

quotes.text: Seems like everyone's an actor / Or they're an actor's best friend / I wonder what was wrong to begin with / That they should all have to pretend

senses.definition: (obsolete, Ancient Rome) An advocate or proctor in civil courts or causes.
(grammar) The subject performing the action of a verb.
(software engineering) The entity that performs a role (in use case analysis).
